title: Wendell and the Extraction
premise: Wren Fairweather, a private security contractor haunted by a botched extraction that killed their team, is hired to shadow a hedge-fund heir named Wendell Ash on a routine flight. Mid-air, every record of the plane's existence is erased by the same shadowy training network that once shaped Wren, revealing Wendell as bait in a scheme to launder a stolen inheritance through Frankfurt's opening bell. Wren must choose between protecting their cover and protecting Wendell, the one client who sees the person beneath the contractor. The story ends with Wren burning the network's ledger at dawn, exposing the erased flight, and walking away from duty into a fragile, chosen life with Wendell.
about_author: N. M. Kavanagh is a former aviation logistics analyst who spent a decade writing risk assessments for clients whose names appeared in no filings. Wendell and the Extraction is their second thriller, written from a farmhouse with deliberately poor cell reception.

chapters.title: The Client Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A sleepless Wren takes a last-minute contract guarding Wendell Ash, a hedge-fund heir flying to Zurich. The emotional beat is numb professionalism cracking slightly at Wendell's odd, disarming honesty about being watched.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Pre-flight checks reveal the charter's tail number belongs to a company dissolved twice. Wren files it away as routine sloppiness, but the reader feels the first cold draft of wrongness.

chapters.title: Wheels Up
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell narrates the takeoff, revealing he suspects his uncles are moving his inheritance offshore without him. His charm masks fear; he hired Wren through a back channel on instinct.

chapters.title: Squawk of Nothing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Over the Alps, the transponder code returns no aircraft, then no flight, then no plane. Radar screens go blank. Wren's old training kicks in with a sick familiarity they can't name yet.

chapters.title: The Incident, Remembered
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, flashback woven into the descent to a military strip. We learn of the extraction two years ago that killed Wren's team, and the training program, called the Ledger, that built them.

chapters.title: Grounded in Nowhere
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. They land at a decommissioned airfield. Wendell's fear sharpens into resolve as Wren admits, against every rule, that the plane has been erased.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Contract
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren discovers the Ledger's signature on the erasure: a handler codenamed Vesper, Wren's old instructor. The beat is betrayal layered on dread.

chapters.title: The Uncle's Call
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell's uncle Marcus calls, warm and wrong, telling him to stay put. Wendell lies for the first time in his life, and feels strangely free.

chapters.title: Fuel, Lies, and Diesel
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They scavenge fuel at the dead airfield while men in unmarked vehicles sweep the perimeter. Wren teaches Wendell to move quietly; the first thread of trust ties itself.

chapters.title: Vesper's Voice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Vesper calls Wren directly, offering reinstatement if Wendell is delivered by Friday's Frankfurt open. Wren says nothing, and the silence is a decision.

chapters.title: Train Through the Tyrol
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The pair moves overland on freight and local rail, bickering, exhausted, alive. The emotional beat is reluctant intimacy between two people pretending this is a job.

chapters.title: The Ledger Explained
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, over cheap wine in Innsbruck. Wren confesses the whole truth: the Ledger trains contractors to be deniable, then erases them when convenient. Wendell doesn't flinch, which undoes Wren more than fear would.

chapters.title: Inheritance as Weapon
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell decodes his grandfather's will: the fortune can only pass if he appears, in person, at a Frankfurt notary before markets open. His disappearance isn't a kidnapping, it's a laundering mechanism.

chapters.title: Safehouse with a View
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A Ledger contact offers shelter and quietly tags them. Wren realizes it too late; the beat is self-recrimination and the first physical closeness between Wren and Wendell, interrupted.

chapters.title: Night Run
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A chase through Munich's rail yards. Wren takes a knife graze protecting Wendell; Wendell stitches the wound with shaking hands. The beat is love arriving without permission.

chapters.title: What Duty Costs
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren contemplates handing Wendell over to save what's left of their old team, held as leverage. The moral floor tilts; duty and love become irreconcilable.

chapters.title: Marcus in Munich
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell confronts Uncle Marcus in a hotel bar, playing the naive heir. He walks out with a copied drive and the knowledge that his family sold his name years ago.

chapters.title: The Drive's Contents
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The drive holds the Ledger's client list: banks, states, and the Frankfurt clearing house that will validate Wendell's stolen inheritance at open. The clock becomes the plot.

chapters.title: Vesper's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Vesper threatens to release the incident file, framing Wren for the team's deaths, unless Wendell is delivered by 08:00. Wren's guilt is weaponized.

chapters.title: Wendell's Choice
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell learns of the ultimatum and offers himself up, believing his appearance at the notary can be turned into testimony. Wren refuses; the argument is the book's thematic heart.

chapters.title: The Old Team
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren contacts a surviving teammate, Ada, who agrees to help, but warns that the Ledger always leaves one survivor to bury the rest. Paranoia becomes method.

chapters.title: Counterfeit Heir
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They prepare a decoy: Wendell's appearance staged at a false notary while the real plan moves. The beat is grim camaraderie and Wren letting others in for the first time since the incident.

chapters.title: Ada's Price
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Ada reveals she's been Ledger all along, or has she? She feeds them a route that feels too clean. Trust becomes a tactical question, not a feeling.

chapters.title: Ambush on the Main
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The decoy route is ambushed; Ada dies covering their escape, her loyalty proven only in death. Wren's grief reopens the incident wound, and this time they don't look away.

chapters.title: Frankfurt at Night
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The city glitters and indifferent. Wendell, for the first time, leads, mapping the clearing house's server floor from childhood memory of his grandfather's office.

chapters.title: The Notary's Back Door
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Recon of the notary reveals Vesper waiting in person, patient as winter. Wren realizes Vesper wanted them in Frankfurt all along, to close the loop personally.

chapters.title: Confession at Dawn's Edge
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In a safehouse stairwell, Wren and Wendell admit what this is: not protection, not duty, love against every instruction either was ever given. Quiet, terrified, certain.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Server Floor
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Infiltration begins. Wren plants Ada's copied access while Wendell walks openly through the front as the heir, every camera his ally. The beat is controlled terror.

chapters.title: Vesper and Wren, Face to Face
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Confrontation in the archive room. Vesper offers the old lie, that erasure is mercy. Wren answers with the incident file, read aloud, names and all.

chapters.title: Wendell at the Notary
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell appears before the notary, claims his inheritance, and immediately signs it into a trust that freezes the laundering chain. The trap reverses; the money becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Burn Before the Bell
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. With minutes to Frankfurt's open, Wren triggers the ledger purge, broadcasting the erased flight, the client list, and the incident file to every regulator on the list. The beat is catharsis through fire.

chapters.title: Markets Open
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The clearing house halts; uncles scatter; Vesper's network unravels in real time as screens light up. Wendell watches his family's empire eat itself and feels not triumph but release.

chapters.title: Vesper's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Vesper, exposed, offers one final choice: disappear together, the old way. Wren declines, choosing to be seen, and walks out as Vesper is taken by people who finally have names.

chapters.title: Aftermath in a Police Station
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Testimony, statements, a sympathetic investigator. For the first time, the system works, imperfectly, because two people forced it to. The beat is exhausted relief.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Decided
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell dissolves the family fund, funds the victims' families, including Wren's lost team, and keeps only the farmhouse his grandfather never mentioned.

chapters.title: Wren's File, Closed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The incident file is officially corrected; the team's names are cleared. Wren sleeps, badly at first, then one whole night through, for the first time in two years.

chapters.title: The Contract Expires
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren formally ends the security contract. Neither asks the other to stay; both do anyway. The beat is tenderness after adrenaline.

chapters.title: Farmhouse, Poor Reception
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Quiet domesticity: repairs, coffee, a garden Wendell is terrible at. Wren keeps a go-bag packed out of habit and, one morning, unpacks it.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Door
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A stranger arrives with a job offer from what's left of the old world. Wren looks at Wendell, at the garden, and says no, and the no costs nothing.

chapters.title: Wendell and the Extraction
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, closing. On the farmhouse porch, Wendell asks what they'll call this story. Wren says it wasn't an extraction; it was an escape they made together. Final image: two names, written side by side, in a record no one can erase.
